propositions: sync and the S3 doctor each implement a merge/reconciliation strategy but share only ~4 lines of graph arithmetic while holding opposed policies on unrelated histories and failure modes

sync.reconverge refuses to merge on a non-empty local store to prevent orphan grafting, while the S3 doctor unions unconditionally (held-out test requirement), making behaviour-preserving unification impossible
sync's consumers read ticket events from worktree files, so a ref-only merge would cause silent staleness; sync cannot adopt the doctor's merge-tree engine without breaking its read path
the targeted code duplication (doctor's worktree git merge policy) was eliminated by Gerrit 1665, which rewrote the doctor to use merge-tree/commit-tree without worktree access
sync must never raise exceptions on merge failure (logs warning instead), while the doctor must raise S3DoctorConflict to signal push abandonment, making failure-policy unification behaviour-changing
